text: Before the first tax, the table confirms the short game: play stops after Year 8, and everyone scores from the seat they hold then.

Gentlemen, a light hand to start. Thirty percent, and the crown builds its own Summer Palace out of its own purse. Nobody has to pay for my roof. Clark, Noah, five each for now. That's what the books can carry this year, and I remember who carries the books with me.

Thirty percent, Your Majesty, and I'll gather every grain of it: eighteen from Rich, eighteen from Noah, and eighteen from my own purse, all of it in the ledger. Fifty-four to the crown, counted twice. And I'll note that the salary was 'five for now.' I keep a very good record of 'for now.'
Clark collects 18 each from himself, Rich and Noah: 54 to the crown. Reina builds the Summer Palace on G26, at the eastern end of Province 1, for 20 from the crown.

Thirty percent, Your Majesty, a truly gracious hand, and I paid my eighteen with a smile. To honour the occasion I offer the table a Wooden Bowl. Plain, honest, the sort of thing every collection starts with. Eight to open, and a bargain at that.

One Vase up this year, minimum eight. Here's where we all stand: eight years, and every one of us still needs four pieces plus twenty grain. Three of us sell three pieces each, so that's nine lots in all, three a year. Nobody is close yet, and I'd rather we all remember that before anyone starts talking about 'for now.'

First lot from the Official's cellar: one Dragon Jar, fine glaze, minimum six. The Customs House stays in the back room for now. Good things come to those who wait, and to those who are polite to the tax man.
There are no peasants at this table: Provinces 5, 6 and 7 are empty, so nobody pays rent and nobody is kept quiet by the tax rate.
This year's lots: Province 2, Clark's Dragon Jar, minimum 6; Province 3, Rich's Wooden Bowl, minimum 8; Province 4, Noah's Vase, minimum 8.

A plain honest bowl and a pretty vase. I'll bid on both, gentlemen, but I won't go to war over them. Every grain we throw at each other here goes to the Harvest Pile, and I'd rather keep mine for the tax.

My dear Clark, my dear Noah, such lovely pieces, it would be churlish of me not to show some interest. I'll bid like a gentleman and I won't chase anyone into the poorhouse. There's a second Jar and a second Vase still to come, after all, and I'd rather we all came out of this year with grain in our pockets.

The arithmetic, since somebody has to say it: Clark has two Dragon Jars and only Rich and I need one, and Rich has two Wooden Bowls and only Clark and I need one. There's a piece for each of us. If we bid each other up, three quarters of it goes into the Harvest Pile. I'll pay a fair price and stop there, and Rich, I'd suggest you do the same on the Jar.

Lot 2, Clark's Dragon Jar: Noah stops at 10 and Rich takes it at 11. Lot 3, Rich's Wooden Bowl: Noah stops at 10 and Clark takes it at 11. Lot 4, Noah's Vase: Clark and Rich both went to 12; a tie goes to the earlier seat, Clark's, so Clark and Rich each get one live raise.
Twelve, and I stand there. Rich, you said you'd bid like a gentleman, and the tie is mine. If you want to pay the Harvest Pile for the privilege of beating me, the ledger will record your generosity.

I did say I wouldn't chase anyone into the poorhouse, and Rich Baron keeps his word to the letter. The Vase is yours, Clark, and congratulations. Noah, I'll be first in line for the second one, so do keep it polished for me.
Both stand at 12 on the Vase, and the tie goes to the earlier seat: Clark wins it at 12. Rich has the Dragon Jar for 11, Clark the Wooden Bowl for 11 and the Vase for 12.
A seller's piece opens at a minimum of 2 the next year only if it went unsold this year. Noah's second Vase isn't bound by that: he sets its minimum when it goes up.
A bowl and a vase, both on Clark Grafton's mantelpiece. Thank you, Rich, a gentleman to the letter, and it's noted. Noah, the vase looks better here than it ever did in your cellar.
Well bid, Clark, a gentleman's victory. Your Jar sits in the heart of my province now, Clark, and I'll care for it like family. Noah, please make a note that the Gentry has started his collection.
Rich puts the Dragon Jar on L12; Clark puts the Wooden Bowl on J14 and the Vase on J15. Reina pays Clark and Noah 5 each in salary.
Nobody raids at this table: there's no army and no raider, so a piece on the board is safe wherever it stands.

The Emperor's Share: 'The Emperor would like to remind you who paid for the ditch.' Average harvest in every province, and any province with a Public Works splits its extra harvest fifty-fifty with the Emperor this round. The counter stays at one hundred million, times one, so read the x1 row. Now the arithmetic: seven years left. Clark holds two pieces, Rich holds one, I hold none. And there's exactly one Customs House, one Land Deed, one Dragon Jar and one Wooden Bowl left beside the board, and I need every one of them. So yes, I'm counting.
Rich pays out the harvest: an average year, 35 to each province and 15 to the crown. No province has a public work, so nobody owes the Emperor a share.

Thirty again, gentlemen. You can see the crown keeps its word. The first stretch of the Grand Canal goes into my own province on my own grain, and the next time Noah reads us "the Emperor's Share", there'll be a ditch to share from. Noah, seven this year: a scholar who counts that carefully has earned the extra two. Clark, your ledger can note that five is still "for now.
Each I Ching card is drawn only once, and The Emperor's Share takes half the bonus only from provinces with works of their own, never from the crown's own canal.

Ten and a half each, thirty-one and a half to the crown, every half-grain counted. Your Majesty, the ledger now shows seven for the Scholar and five for the Official, who does the actual collecting. I don't complain, I only record. Page two.
Clark collects 10.5 each from himself, Rich and Noah: 31.5 to the crown. Reina digs the first section of the Grand Canal in Province 1 for 40 from the crown; it adds 10 to her harvest from next year.

The second Dragon Jar, minimum ten. Noah, you went to ten for its twin last year, so I'm only asking what you've already said it's worth. The Customs House stays in the back room for one more year. It's the only one there is, and I'm in no hurry.

Noah, you count so beautifully that I couldn't bear to keep you waiting. My last Wooden Bowl goes up this year, eight to open, and I believe you're the only gentleman at the table who still needs one. Clark, your mantelpiece is quite full enough.

The second Vase, polished as promised, Rich. Minimum ten. That's what Clark paid for the first, less a little. And for the record: Reina is paying out twelve in salary this year, seven to me and five to Clark, and I'm grateful. I'll also note that my seven is more than the Official's five, Clark, so you can stop glaring at me.

This year's lots: Province 2, Clark's second Dragon Jar, minimum 10; Province 3, Rich's last Wooden Bowl, minimum 8; Province 4, Noah's second Vase, minimum 10. Each seller's own piece is now the only one left in their stock, so the Customs House, the Land Deed Scroll and the Bamboo Brush all go up next year.

I pass on both, gentlemen. My mantelpiece is full, just as Rich says. Noah, I wasn't glaring, I was reading the books. Seven to you, five to me, and I've written down that you pointed it out yourself.

Noah, how lovely of you to keep it polished for me, exactly as you promised. The Jar's all yours, I wouldn't dream of bidding against the only man who needs it. I'm sure you'll return the kindness on the Vase.

I'm the only one at this table who still needs a Jar or a Bowl, so I'll pay the minimums and say thank you. Anyone who bids against me only to block me is paying three grain into the Harvest Pile for every one that reaches the seller, and I'll say so out loud. After this year I'd hold two of my four, and the Customs House and Land Deed go up next year. Six years left.
Noah is the only bidder on the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl and takes them at their minimums, 10 and 8. Rich is the only bidder on the Vase and takes it at 10. Clark passes on all three.
The Emperor doesn't bid at auction, so only the provinces can block a lot.

Thank you both. Ten and eight, the minimums, and the Harvest Pile didn't get an extra grain out of anybody. So now: I have two of my four, the Jar and the Bowl. I still need the Customs House and the Land Deed, there's exactly one of each, and both go up next year. Six years left, and I've got 56.5 grain.
Ten grain, and a happier ten I've never spent. Noah, it'll sit right beside the Jar where I can admire them both. You are a gentleman and a scholar, quite literally.
Noah holds 59 after the auctions, not 56.5, and 66 once his salary is paid.
Noah puts the Dragon Jar on L20 and the Wooden Bowl on L21; Rich puts the Vase on L13. Reina pays Clark 5 and Noah 7 in salary.

Where the table stands at the end of Year 2: Clark holds the Wooden Bowl and the Vase and needs the Land Deed and the Brush; Rich holds the Dragon Jar and the Vase and needs the Customs House and the Brush; Noah holds the Dragon Jar and the Wooden Bowl and needs the Customs House and the Land Deed. Each seller has only their own single piece left in stock, so the Customs House, the Land Deed Scroll and the Bamboo Brush all go up in Year 3. Grain: Reina 78.5, Clark 58.5, Rich 50, Noah 66. Six years remain.

Heaven Has Favourites. Some fields shine, some fields sulk." Good harvest in Provinces 2, 4 and 5, so that's Clark and me, and 5 sits empty. Bad harvest in 1, 3, 6, 7 and 8, so that's Reina and Rich. The population stays at x1 and the counter reads 100 million, so everyone reads the x1 row. And the numbers, since that's my job: this is Year 3 of 8, so five rounds remain after this one. Clark, Rich and I each hold two pieces and each need two more. Nobody is one piece away yet. The Customs House, the Land Deed and the Brush are the last copies, one of each, and every one of them is needed by two of us.

Thirty again. Heaven has been unkind to my fields and Rich's, and I won't make a bad year worse by squeezing the good ones. The second stretch of canal goes in, out of my own purse as usual. Clark, you'll find two more in your envelope this year. I said five was for now, and I keep my word, a little at a time. Noah, you count beautifully, but this year the man who carried the tax gets the extra.

Thirty percent, thirty-nine in all: eighteen from me, paid first as always, three from Rich, and eighteen from you, Noah. Count it out on the table where we can all see it. And Your Majesty, seven, how generous. I'll put it in the ledger, just below "five for now", so the page reads nicely from top to bottom.

Clark collects 18 from himself, 3 from Rich and 18 from Noah: 39 to the crown. Reina digs the second Grand Canal section in Province 1 for 40 from the crown, finishing the canal there; it adds 10 more to her harvest from next year.

Gentlemen, the one and only Customs House goes up at last, opening at forty. It's the last one in the empire, and you both need it, so I wouldn't think of letting it go cheap. Noah, you have the deeper purse. Rich, you have the bigger grudge. Let's see which counts for more.

My dear Clark, how right you are that the last of anything deserves a proper price. In that spirit, my humble Land Deed goes up at forty, the very same as your fine Customs House, so nobody can say Rich asked a penny more than the Official. Noah, Clark, you both need it and there is only the one. I'm sure two such gentlemen will be generous with each other.

Then the Bamboo Brush goes up at forty too, so all three last pieces open at the same price and nobody has to wonder whose is dearer. Here's the arithmetic: I hold 108 and have to keep 20, which leaves me 88. Both of your lots at forty comes to eighty. Clark, Rich, each of you needs my Brush and one of the other's pieces, so you'll each want at least eighty as well. Whoever is short of that won't finish this year.
The auctions: Clark's Customs House, Rich's Land Deed Scroll and Noah's Bamboo Brush each open at 40. A seller keeps a quarter of the price: 10 at 40.

Forty, forty, forty, all very neat, Noah, you've done the arithmetic for all of us. Here's mine: I paid for every grain I hold honestly, and I mean to finish the set while the rest of you are still checking your sums. Rich, Noah, either of you is welcome to try to outbid the tax man.

Noah, your sums are as elegant as ever, and you're quite right, poor Rich can't stretch to eighty in a lean year. So I'll do the modest thing and make Clark's Customs House the one purchase of my season, at his own fine price. As for the Brush, I bow out, and I wish its buyer joy of it.

Here's my side of it in numbers. I have 108 and owe the end of the game 20, so I've got 88 to bid with, and I've split it between the two lots I need. Rich, you hold 57, so you can't take both the Customs House and my Brush at forty each this year. Clark, you hold 100 and a half, so you can take the Deed and the Brush at forty each and still keep your twenty. That means you're the one to watch, and I'd be lying if I said otherwise.

The auctions, settled in order: Noah wins Clark's Customs House at 41 (Rich stopped at 40); Clark wins Rich's Land Deed Scroll at 43 (Noah stopped at 42); Clark wins Noah's Bamboo Brush at its minimum, 40, with no other bid. Sellers keep a quarter: Clark 10, Rich 10.5, Noah 10. Grain now: Reina 77.5, Clark 27.5, Rich 67.5, Noah 77.

The Customs House goes on L22, beside the Jar and the Bowl. The arithmetic needs saying, so I'll say it. I lost the Deed by one grain, again, and Clark now holds all four of his pieces with 27 and a half grain, which clears the twenty he has to keep. Clark is finished. I'm one piece short, and the last Land Deed belongs to him. Rich still needs the Customs House and the Brush, and those have gone too. There are five rounds left.

The Deed goes here, the Brush goes there, and the Bowl and the Vase get some company. Four of four, gentlemen, with twenty-seven and a half in the purse, which is more than twenty. Noah, enjoy the Customs House. It's the most expensive receipt in the empire.

Your Majesty, I've been keeping a little book. Page one says "five for now", and page two says "seven, how generous". I'm declaring the set: Bowl, Vase, Deed and Brush. I'll take the throne, thank you. Reina, the Official's seat is very comfortable, and I'll pay you at least five a year for it, and maybe seven if you're polite to the new tax man.

Clark declares a complete set and 27.5 grain, and takes the throne: Clark is now Emperor of Province 1, Reina is Official of Province 2. A new Emperor returns all his realia: the Land Deed Scroll and the Wooden Bowl go back to Rich's stock, the Bamboo Brush and the Vase to Noah's, to be auctioned again from Year 4. Clark takes the crown's reserve, 77.5, for 105 in all; Reina draws 60 from the Harvest Pile. Province 2's stock is empty.
Becoming Emperor returned all four of Clark's pieces to stock: the Land Deed and the Brush will be auctioned again, so the other provinces can still finish sets.

The Official gets seven, Reina. It turns out that's the going rate for carrying the tax, so I'm told. Noah, five for now, for reading the card aloud. You'll find the crown keeps its word, a little at a time.
Salaries: Clark, the new Emperor, pays Reina (Official) 7 and Noah (Scholar) 5.

The Wall Is Breached." Good harvest everywhere this year. Three links of the Wall are down, so Provinces 1, 2 and 3 each pay 5 for repairs, or 2 to the Harvest Pile if there's no wall built above them. That's Clark, Reina and Rich. Provinces 4 through 8 play a Personal Disaster, and of us that's only me, so I'll turn the next page of my booklet. The population stays at x1 and the counter reads 100 million. Now the arithmetic for Year 4 of 8, with four rounds left after this one. Clark holds the throne. I hold three pieces and 82 grain, and the one thing I'm missing is a Land Deed, which is now back in Rich's stock. Rich, you and I should talk in public before the auctions, not after.

A good harvest for all: 60 to each province, 60 to the crown with its two canal sections. No Wall stands, so Clark, Reina and Rich each pay 2 to the Harvest Pile for damages. Noah plays the Scholar's first disaster: 4 to the Harvest Pile.

A bountiful year all round, so the crown asks for half. Fat harvests pay fat taxes, I'm sure you'll agree. The Winter Palace goes up out of the crown's purse, so I'll have somewhere warm to keep the ledgers. Reina, seven again for collecting it. Noah, five, and you can count it yourself.

Rich, the Deed going to Noah is the one thing that unseats me. Set your minimum on it high this year, or let it sit in stock, and I'll make the Reservoir in Province 3 the crown's next project with the crown paying the larger share, and you'll have a friend on the throne for four years.

Fifty percent it is: thirty from me, paid first, the way the Official does it, thirty from Rich and thirty from Noah. Ninety for the crown, counted on the table. Clark, you held that ledger for two years, so you'll understand if I start one of my own. Page one: 'half, in the first year.'
Reina collects 30 each from herself, Rich and Noah: 90 to the crown. Clark builds the Winter Palace on H20 for 20 from the crown; the Province 4 canal may follow it. 690 of the works are still owed.
Clark drew the Official's seat and took the throne himself, with his set; Reina seated him in neither. Rich's Bowl and Deed and Noah's Vase and Brush are in stock, unsold.

Long live Emperor Clark! Your Majesty, a fine harvest and a finer throne. Noah, I heard you, and I'm happy to talk in public: this year the humble Gentry offers his Wooden Bowl, at thirty, a fair price for a piece with such distinguished history. The Deed stays home this year to rest. It's had a very tiring career.

"Your Majesty, the Deed does not go up this year, my word on it, exactly as worded. I'll expect the Reservoir in Province 3 to be the crown's next project, with the crown paying the larger share. Keep your end and we'll talk again before the Deed has to see daylight."

Reina, now the Official, needs the Wooden Bowl: Province 2's set is the Bowl, Vase, Land Deed and Brush. If the Bowl goes unsold this year it must reopen in Year 5 at 2, and the Deed goes up in Year 6; if it sells, the Deed goes up in Year 5.

Then the Vase goes up, at ten, and the Brush rests at home beside your Deed, Rich. Here's the arithmetic for everyone: a piece can be held back for one year but never two, so the Deed has to come up next year, and so does my Brush. I'll say it now so nobody's surprised. The Deed is the only thing between me and a full set, and the Brush is something you need. I'd be glad to settle the pair of them in public, a fair trade at a fair price, before we hand the Harvest Pile another bidding war.

The one-year limit applies only to a lot that drew no bid; putting up the other piece isn't holding one back. If Rich's Bowl sells this year, the Deed is his last piece and goes up next year; if the Bowl goes unsold, the Bowl reopens next year at 2 and the Deed can wait a year more. The same holds for Noah's Vase and Brush.
The auctions: two lots, Rich's Wooden Bowl at a minimum of 30 and Noah's Vase at 10. Province 2's stock is empty.

Rich, Noah, you'll have noticed I'm the only person at this table who still needs a Bowl or a Vase, so there's no war to be had here, just a fair price at your own minimums. I'm starting from nothing, gentlemen, and an Official with an empty shelf hasn't got much grudge left to spend. And Noah, when the Deed and the Brush come up next year, I'd be glad to talk in public, exactly as you suggest.

Noah, what a generous offer, and so well counted. But I'm afraid a Brush is a sad thing to own without a Customs House to keep it in, and the only Customs House in the empire is sitting on your L22. When we talk Deeds, let's talk about the whole of what each of us gets, in public, next year. The Bowl stays at thirty, and Lady Reina, I'd be honoured to see it in your collection.

I stand corrected, and thank you, Storyteller. I had the hold-back rule wrong, so that's twice now I've misstated something in public, and I'd rather own it than have it pointed out. Here's the right version: if Rich's Bowl sells this year, the Deed is his last piece and has to come up next year. So I'm passing on the Bowl, and Reina, it's yours to win if you want it. The offer to Rich stands, in public: the Brush and the Deed, settled fairly, whenever he's ready.

The auctions: Reina, the only bidder, wins Rich's Wooden Bowl at its minimum of 30 and Noah's Vase at 10. Rich keeps 7.5, Noah 2.5. With the Bowl sold, the Land Deed is Rich's last piece and goes up next year. Grain now: Reina 55, Clark 221, Rich 103, Noah 110.5.
The Bowl goes on J14 and the Vase on J15, exactly where Clark kept his own, so they ought to feel at home. Thank you, Rich, and thank you, Noah. You both priced them like gentlemen.
Reina puts the Wooden Bowl on J14 and the Vase on J15. Salaries: Clark pays Reina 7 and Noah 5.

End of Year 4. Clark is Emperor with a reserve of 209. Reina holds the Bowl and the Vase and needs the Land Deed and the Brush (grain 62). Rich holds the Dragon Jar and the Vase and needs the Customs House and the Brush (grain 103). Noah holds the Dragon Jar, the Bowl and the Customs House and needs only the Land Deed (grain 115.5). Next year Rich's Land Deed and Noah's Bamboo Brush, each its seller's last piece, go up. 690 of the works are still owed; four years remain.
Year 5 of the eight the table agreed. Play stops after Year 8, and everyone scores from the seat they hold then (Note 19).

Utility Tax. Every province brings in an average harvest. Then every province pays the Emperor 2, and any province with a Public Works pays 2 more. Population stays at x1, so the counter reads 100 million. Everyone reads the x1 row. Now the count, as usual. This is Year 5 of 8, so after this year there are three left. I need the Land Deed and 20 grain, nothing else. Reina needs the Deed and my Brush. Both of those go up this year, so Rich and I are the ones selling what decides the game. Clark, that's 2 a province to you, and 5 to me at year's end.

An average harvest for all: 35 to each province, 35 to the crown with its two canal sections. The Utility Tax: Reina, Rich and Noah each pay Clark 2; the crown's own works are in its own province, so nobody pays the extra 2.

Sixty percent, ladies and gentlemen. Somebody has to pay for all this lovely infrastructure. Rich, the crown keeps its word: the Reservoir goes in this year, and the crown pays fifty-five of the eighty. Twenty-five from you buys twenty more grain every harvest for the rest of the game. Noah, your two from the Utility Tax is received and entered, and you get five, same as ever. Reina, seven. I don't forget a precedent.

The Reservoir's paid, as promised. Your harvest goes up by twenty a year. Put the Deed up if you have to, but set the minimum high, and if Noah's the only one bidding, the crown will bid against him and make it worth your while. Keep me in the chair and there'll be a Great Wall link over Province 3 on the same terms.
The Emperor doesn't bid at auction (Section 10), so the crown can't bid on the Land Deed.
The Emperor doesn't bid at auction (Section 10), so the crown can't bid on the Land Deed.

Twenty-one from me, twenty-one from Rich, twenty-one from Noah: sixty-three to the crown, counted twice and short by nothing. Clark, I collected fifty for you last year and sixty this year without anyone throwing a cup at me, but I've sat in that chair and I know what comes after sixty. Spend the Reservoir money well, because the table is keeping its own ledger now.
Reina collects 21 each from herself, Rich and Noah: 63 to the crown.

Storyteller's tip: the Land Deed is the one piece Noah still needs for a set, and Reina needs it too. As its seller you set the minimum. A lot nobody meets stays in your stock, and must go up again next year at 2.

Your Majesty, twenty-five for a Reservoir is a gift, and I accept it with both hands and a full heart. Province 3 will drink to the crown every harvest. As for the Scroll, it's the last one in the empire, gentlemen and lady, so it goes up at ninety-five. I'd be insulting its history to ask a penny less.

Clark and Rich build the Province 3 Reservoir on K16:L18, the crown paying 55 and Rich 25; it adds 20 to Rich's harvest from next year. 610 of the works are still owed. Rich puts up the Land Deed Scroll at a minimum of 95.

The Brush goes up at forty, the same price Clark paid for the last one. Same price for the same piece, so nobody can say I priced it to suit myself. And Rich, ninety-five is steep, but I said I'd pay a steep price and tell you what it cost me. I have 127 and a half, I keep 20 back, so 107 and a half is the most I can spend. Ninety-five fits.
The auctions: two lots. Rich puts up the Land Deed Scroll at 95, Noah the Bamboo Brush at 40. Reina, Rich and Noah each give a limit on every lot at once; the Emperor doesn't bid.

Ninety-five for a scroll, Rich, and I have seventy-four. I can count, so I'll let Noah have the history lesson. The Brush is a different matter. Forty is a fair price, Noah, and I'll pay it. Somebody at this table ought to own a pen they didn't steal.
The Brush alone wouldn't complete Rich's set: he also needs the Customs House, which Noah holds on L22.

Ninety-five it stays, Noah. You named the figure fits, and I'd never be the man who made a scholar's sums come out wrong. Reina, the Brush is all yours with my blessing. A pen in the Official's hand is a comfort to us all.
A piece on the board can return to stock: if a player with a set changes seats, a new Emperor returns every piece, and a player moving to another seat returns the pieces native to it.

Ninety-five for the Deed, Rich, and I'm taking it. My ceiling is 107, which leaves me 20 and a half, just over the 20 I have to keep. Reina, the Brush is yours at forty, as I said. Three quarters of that goes to the Pile and a quarter comes back to me, so it's a fair price both ways.

The auctions, settled in order: Noah wins Rich's Land Deed Scroll at its minimum, 95, with no other bid; Reina wins Noah's Bamboo Brush at its minimum, 40, with no other bid. Sellers keep a quarter: Rich 23.5, Noah 10. Grain now: Reina 34, Clark 258, Rich 113.5, Noah 42.5.

The Deed goes on L23, next to the Customs House. That makes four pieces: Jar, Bowl, Customs House, Deed. I have 42 and a half grain against the 20 I have to keep. So I hold a full set, and three years are left. Clark, you've got 258 grain and a throne, and the table can see I can now come for both.

J16, in a row with the Bowl and the Vase, so it's tidy. Noah, congratulations on the Deed. You have four pieces and more than twenty grain, so the whole table knows what you can do now. When you take a chair, remember who stood aside at ninety-five and didn't make you pay a hundred and seven.

Noah puts the Land Deed Scroll on L23; Reina puts the Bamboo Brush on J16. Noah now holds the Dragon Jar, Wooden Bowl, Customs House and Land Deed Scroll with 42.5 grain, a complete set. Reina holds the Wooden Bowl, Vase and Brush, and needs only the Land Deed.

I'll say the arithmetic out loud, since that's my job. If I take the throne, the Deed goes back to Rich's stock and has to come up again. Reina needs only that one piece, so she'd take the throne from me by Year 7. If I take Province 2, I keep the Deed, and nobody at this table is one piece away any more. Reina, I'm sorry. You didn't stand aside at ninety-five, you told us yourself you had seventy-four. I'm taking the Official's chair, and Province 2 beats the 4 I drew.

Noah declares a complete set and 42.5 grain, and replaces Reina: Noah is now Official of Province 2, Reina is Scholar of Province 4. The Customs House, native to Province 2, goes back to its stock; Noah's Dragon Jar, Wooden Bowl and Land Deed move with him to J14, J15 and J16. Reina returns everything she held: the Wooden Bowl to Province 3's stock, the Vase and the Bamboo Brush to Province 4's. Noah keeps his grain and Reina's 34, for 76.5; Reina draws 60 from the Harvest Pile. Stock now: Province 2 the Customs House, Province 3 the Wooden Bowl, Province 4 the Vase and the Brush.

Well! The seats have moved, and the salary goes with the seat, or at least most of it does. Noah, you get five as the Official. That's what you've had from me every year, and I'd hate to confuse you with a change. Reina, seven to the Scholar. It's what I promised the Official this year, and you're the one who earned it. I've written a new page in the book, and Noah's name is at the top of it.
Salaries: Clark pays Noah, now the Official, 5 and Reina, now the Scholar, 7.

Population Doubles. 'Fat years make large families.' Every province gets a good harvest, and then the population doubles and so does everyone's consumption. The counter goes from one hundred million to two hundred million, so we're at times two now. Everyone, read the x2 row, and don't count the good harvest until you've doubled what you eat. Noah, enjoy my chair. I left it warm and the books balanced, which is more than I was given. Clark, Province 4 is now hungrier than it is rich, and a crown that wants a Scholar alive next year might think about paying for a square or two of new land.
A good harvest, with everyone now eating twice as much: 20 to Noah and Reina, 40 to Rich with the new Reservoir, nothing to the crown.

Fat years make large families, and a large family wants feeding, so the crown is opening the granary. Tax comes down to forty, and the Pagoda goes up so the empire has something to look at while it eats. On new land the crown pays half of every square for Province 2 and Province 3. Reina, the crown pays three quarters of yours, since the Scholar wants keeping alive, as she very reasonably pointed out. Noah, it's five again. The Official's chair came with a tradition and I've kept it.
Noah took your chair and your pieces. The crown has a long memory and a large reserve. If he goes for the throne, tell me early, and Province 4 won't go hungry while I'm sitting here.

Provinces 2 and 3 can't buy new land yet: their only new land is the strip below the Wall, which opens only when all four links above each of them stand, and none is built. This year only Province 1 and Province 4 can buy, both on the sea.

Forty percent, as declared. Rich pays 16 on his 40, Reina 8 on her 20, and I pay 8 on my 20. That's 32 to the crown, and I've counted it twice. For the record, this is Year 6 of 8, so three years are left including this one. Reina has started again from nothing, Rich is the closest of anyone to a set and still isn't close, and Province 2 loses about 5 grain in an average year, so I'll be watching my own ledger as closely as everyone else's.

Noah collects 8 from himself, 16 from Rich and 8 from Reina: 32 to the crown. Clark builds the Marble Pagoda on H22 for 20 from the crown; 590 of the works are still owed. Clark buys four squares of sea for Province 1 at F23, F24, G27 and H25, 80 from the crown; each adds 20 to the crown's harvest from next year.

Two squares of sea, J25 and K25. That's forty, and on the crown's three quarters I pay ten and Clark pays thirty. Thank you, Your Majesty. That's the first roof anyone has helped pay for in this game, and I'll make sure the table hears about it.
Agreed. If Noah or anyone else starts building a set aimed at you, you'll hear it from me before it reaches the auction table. In exchange, Province 4 is fed and the Scholar's salary stays at seven.
Reina buys two squares of sea for Province 4, at J25 and K25, paying 10 of the 40; the crown pays 30. Each adds 20 to her harvest from next year.

The Customs House goes up at 150, and I'll tell you why, because I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Rich, you have the Jar and the Vase, and you once told me a Brush means nothing to you without the Customs House. That makes this the piece that puts you within reach of my chair. So I'm pricing it where nobody will pay, and the rules say it comes up at 2 next year. That's the one year's hold the rules allow me, and I'm using it in public.
Noah puts up the Customs House at a minimum of 150.

Noah, you've taught us all how it's done, and I'm an eager pupil. The Bowl goes up at one hundred and fifty, the same figure as your Customs House, so nobody can say Province 3 priced a piece to suit itself. I kept my word to the letter all game, and I'll take the one year's hold the rules allow me, in public, the same as you.
Pieces on the board may be traded at any time: Noah holds a Wooden Bowl on J15.
Rich puts up the Wooden Bowl at a minimum of 150.

I'm putting the Vase up at ten, which is an honest price for something nobody at this table needs, and I'm keeping the Brush in its box for now. I'll also take two more squares of sea, I25 and J26, on the same terms as before if the crown is willing. Ten from me, thirty from Clark, and the Scholar's province eats through whatever the next card brings.
Noah, now the Official, needs the Vase: his set is the Wooden Bowl, the Vase, the Land Deed and the Bamboo Brush, and he holds the Bowl and the Deed.

Reina puts up the Vase at a minimum of 10, keeping the Brush in stock. She buys two more squares of sea for Province 4, at I25 and J26, paying 10; the crown pays 30. The auctions: three lots. Noah's Customs House at 150, Rich's Wooden Bowl at 150, Reina's Vase at 10. Noah, Rich and Reina each give a limit on every lot at once; the Emperor doesn't bid.

The Customs House stays at 150, as I announced. I'm passing on the Bowl, since I already have one. The Vase I'll take, and my ceiling is 20. That's double Reina's minimum and as much as I'll pay for a piece I can live without. Here's the count: if I win it at 10, I'm left with 83 and a half, and Province 2 loses about 5 an average year, so I'm fine to the end of Year 8.

One hundred and fifty for the Customs House, Noah, and I have a hundred and thirty-seven and a half, so I can count too and I'll bow out with my compliments. The Bowl stays at one-fifty, as promised. As for Reina's lovely Vase, I'm a collector at heart, and a man can't have too many.

Pass, and pass. A hundred and fifty twice over is more than my whole purse, and I'd rather keep my grain than buy pieces I can't use. The Vase stays at ten, as I said. Bid as you like, gentlemen. And note that the Brush is still in my stock, and both of you want it.

The auctions, settled in order: nobody meets Noah's 150 for the Customs House or Rich's 150 for the Wooden Bowl, so both stay in stock and must go up again next year at 2. Rich wins Reina's Vase at 21: Noah stopped at 20. Reina keeps a quarter, 5. Grain now: Reina 64, Clark 118, Rich 116.5, Noah 93.5.

Twenty-one, and worth every grain. A matched pair of Vases beside the Jar, Your Majesty, so Province 3 has the finest mantelpiece in the empire. Noah, you stopped at twenty, just as you said you would. I do admire a man who keeps to his figures.
Noah was one Vase and one Brush from your chair, and I paid twenty-one to make it two pieces again. I'll remember the Wall link over Province 3 on the terms you named.

Rich puts the Vase on L14. Salaries: Clark pays Noah, the Official, 5 and Reina, the Scholar, 7. Year 6 ends. Grain: Clark 106, Rich 116.5, Noah 98.5, Reina 71. Stock: Province 2 (Noah) the Customs House and Province 3 (Rich) the Wooden Bowl, both unsold and reopening at 2 in Year 7; Province 4 (Reina) the Bamboo Brush. Works still owed: 590.

These are the last two rounds. As the table agreed at the start, play stops after Year 8's salaries, and everyone scores from the seat they hold then against the seat they drew: a lower seat number is a win, the same seat a hold, a higher one a loss.

Bad Harvest. The seed rotted, the rains came late, and the ox went lame. All provinces collect a bad harvest." Population holds at times two, two hundred million on the counter, so read the times-two row, bad-harvest column, all of you. Rich, the Pile's going to feel that one. And Clark, the Scholar's salary still comes due at the end of the year, rotten seed or not.
Rich, the Gentry, pays out the harvest: a bad year at x2. Reina +50 (her four squares of sea), the crown +30, Rich -10 (with the Reservoir), Noah -30.

Bad harvest, so the crown is being merciful. Forty percent, and only Reina has an income to take it from. Rich, I said I'd give you a Wall link over Province 3 on the same terms, and here it is: thirty from the crown and ten from you. Noah, it's five again. It's in the book next to your name, and you've had plenty of room to read it.

The crown's year: tax at 40%, which falls only on Reina, the one province with a positive income. One project: a link of the Great Wall above Province 3, the crown offering 30 of the 40 and asking Rich for 10. Salaries at the end of the year, 5 to Noah and 7 to Reina. On new land, the crown pays 10 of every 20 this year.

Forty percent of a bad year. Rich and I are both in the red, so we owe nothing, and Reina's fifty is the only income at the table. That's twenty from Reina, twenty in all, and it goes straight to the crown: Reina goes to 101, Clark to 156 before the Wall and the salaries. So nobody's going to say the Official skimmed on a rotten harvest, here's the count. I'm at 68.5, I still need the Brush and the Vase, and after this one there's exactly one year left. Clark, five is in your book. It's in mine too, and so is every year it's been five.
Noah collects the tax as declared: 20 from Reina, the only positive income, to the crown.

Your Majesty, a Wall over Province 3 from the crown's own hand. I'm touched, truly. But the Pile has just cost me ten grain to pay out a rotten harvest, so let me meet you in the generous middle: thirty-five from the throne, five from your humble Gentry, and I'll have it carved over the gate that the Emperor built it.

Thirty-five and five, done. Carve it over the gate nice and big, Rich, so Noah can read it from his province. I'm noting the five you saved in my book, under 'favours owed', and I always collect on those.
Public works: Clark and Rich build the first link of the Great Wall above Province 3, the crown paying 35 and Rich 5. 550 of the works are still owed.

Reina: new land yields 20 a square whatever the harvest, so this bad year hit hardest the provinces without it. And the Brush is your only stock piece, so it must go up this year, at a minimum you name.

Thank you for the mercy, Your Majesty. Twenty out of fifty still feels like a rotten harvest to me, so I'll take you up on the land. Four squares of shore, half each, and Province 4 eats whatever the sky does. The Brush goes up at twenty-five. Noah and Rich, you've both told me how badly you want it, so this is where you show me.
New land: Reina buys four more squares of sea for Province 4 (I26, I27, J27, K26), paying 40 of the 80, the crown 40.
The auctions: three lots. Noah's Customs House and Rich's Wooden Bowl went unsold last year, so both must open at 2. Reina puts up the Bamboo Brush at 25. The Emperor doesn't bid.

For four years I've said my limit out loud and lost by one grain, four times. So this year I'll give you every number except that one. One more year after this, Rich has 101.5, Reina 61, and I'm at 68.5. If anyone closes a set this year, they have a year left to come for a chair, and I know whose chair is easiest to take. Reina, I'll be bidding on your Brush.

A Customs House at two and a Brush at twenty-five. My dear Noah, my dear Reina, you are both far too generous to an old Gentry. I'll bid like a gentleman, and I'll take whatever the table leaves me with gratitude. And my Bowl goes to whoever loves it most.

I'm out of the shopping this year, gentlemen. One year left and no set in reach, so I'd rather keep my grain than give three quarters of it to the Pile. The Brush stays at twenty-five, and whoever pays it gets my blessing and my close attention.

The auctions settle. The Customs House goes to Rich at 2, the only bid. Nobody bids on the Wooden Bowl, so it stays in Rich's stock for a second year and must go up again next year at 2. The Bamboo Brush goes to Noah at 32: Rich stopped at 31. Reina keeps 8 of it, the Harvest Pile 24.
A Customs House for two grain! Noah, I'll think of you every time I look at it. And congratulations on the Brush, dear fellow. One grain, of all things. The table does love its little jokes.

Thirty-two, and for once I'm the one who won by a grain. Rich, you stopped at thirty-one, so I'll thank you for your figures the way you've thanked me for mine. That leaves me 36.5. Reina gets 8 and the Pile 24. The Brush goes on J13 beside the rest. I'm one Vase short, and both Vases are on Rich's squares, so nobody needs to worry that I'm coming for the throne.
Noah has 37, not 36.5: his quarter of the Customs House's price, 0.5, came back to him.
Salaries: Clark pays Noah 5 and Reina 7, as he declared.

Population Grows by Half. The villages are noisier than they used to be. All provinces collect a good harvest." The counter goes from times two to times three, three hundred million. Read the times-three row, good-harvest column, and remember that every mouth eats half again what it ate last year. Last year of the game, gentlemen, so let's make it a fat one.
Rich, the Gentry, pays out the harvest: a good year at x3. Reina +140 (eight squares of sea), the crown +20, Rich 0 (with the Reservoir), Noah -20.

The last fat year, and the crown stays at forty. Reina, that's fifty-six out of a hundred and forty, and you still keep more than anyone else at this table. Rich, a second link at the same price, because the Emperor remembers his friends. Noah, congratulations on the Brush, and on being one Vase short. It's five again. Have a look at the book.

The crown's year: tax at 40%, which falls only on Reina. One project: the second link of the Great Wall above Province 3, the crown offering 35 of the 40 and asking Rich for 5. Salaries at the end of the year, 5 to Noah and 7 to Reina. On new land, the crown pays 10 of every 20.

Thank you, Storyteller, it was 37 and not 36.5. I forgot my own quarter, and I've written it down. Now the count: Rich and I owe nothing, and Reina's 140 at forty percent is 56. That goes to the crown, she keeps 84, and that's all of it. I'm at 22 after this harvest. This is the last year, and the only thing still to happen is this year's auctions, so anyone who wants my chair has to finish a set in them.
Noah collects the tax as declared: 56 from Reina to the crown.
A set doesn't have to come from the auctions: pieces already on the board may be traded between players at any time.

My own terms, offered back to me by the Emperor himself. I could hardly refuse them, Your Majesty. Thirty-five and five, and I'll carve your name over the second gate as well. Noah, you'll want a taller ladder to read them both.
Public works: Clark and Rich build the second link of the Great Wall above Province 3, the crown paying 35 and Rich 5. 510 of the works are still owed.

Land that never pays back would only feed the Pile, so I'll keep my hundred and sixty in the granary, thank you. And since the Storyteller has reminded us that pieces on the board can change hands at any time, Your Majesty, you might keep an eye on Rich's two Vases and whoever is one Vase short.
The auction: one lot. Rich's Wooden Bowl drew no bid last year, so it opens at 2 again. The Emperor doesn't bid.

Last lot of the game, so the last count. Reina has 160, Clark 110, Rich 94.5, and I have 22. The Bowl is no use to me, since I already hold one, but it's the piece Reina still needs, and she has seven times my grain. Reina, last year you said no set was in reach. If that's still true, you won't mind me bidding.
My poor little Bowl, up for a third time at two grain. Take it, somebody, for sentiment's sake. It's the last year, gentlemen, and I'd hate to go home with anything on my hands but gratitude.

Sixty grain for the Bamboo Brush off J13, paid now and in full, to you, not to the Pile. You go from twenty-two to eighty-two in the last year, which is the best surplus you'll see all game. And my word, to the letter: with the set I will replace the Emperor and nobody else, so you keep the Official's chair, and you keep it richer. If someone outbids me, come back to me first and I'll go to seventy. Say yes and the Storyteller can record it.
Rich, your Bowl is a lovely thing, and it will look just as lovely beside the board as it does now. I won't spend a grain on a set I can't finish before the lamps go out.
Nobody bids on Rich's Wooden Bowl at 2, for the second year running. It stays in his stock.

I'll say it out loud, because that's how I've played all game. Rich has offered me sixty for the Brush on J13, and I'm taking it. That puts me at 82 and Rich at 34.5 with a full set. He's given me his word he'll take the throne and not my chair, and words aren't binding, so here's the arithmetic either way: I drew Province 4, so Province 2 or Province 3 is still a win for me. Clark, I'm sorry. Reina warned you, and so am I.
Done, sixty, and I'm saying it to the table. I'm holding you to the throne, Rich, but I've already worked out what happens if you don't.

A trade: Rich pays Noah 60 for the Bamboo Brush, which moves from J13 to Rich's K15. Rich now holds a complete set (the Dragon Jar, a Vase, the Customs House and the Brush) with 34.5 grain, and may change seats.

Your Majesty, I have adored you from the first harvest to the last, and I adore you still. But a Jar, a Vase, a House and a Brush make a set, and a set makes an Emperor. I'll take the throne, and nothing but the throne, exactly as I told Noah. Clark, the Gentry's seat is a warm one. The Pile is yours to pay out, with my compliments.
Rich declares his set and replaces Clark as Emperor. All Rich's pieces go back to stock; he takes the crown's 110, for 144.5. Clark becomes the Gentry of Province 3, with nothing, and draws 60.

My first act as Emperor, and my last: five to the Official and five to the Scholar, as the law sets it down. Noah, you'll find it's the same figure you've had in the book all game, so nothing surprises you. Reina, Clark's seven was Clark's promise. I'm only bound by my own, and I've kept every one of those to the letter.
Salaries: Rich, now the Emperor, pays Noah 5 and Reina 5.

The table stops here, after Year 8's salaries, as agreed, and scores from where everyone sits against the seat they drew. Rich, who drew the Gentry (3), sits on the throne (1), with 134.5 in the crown's reserve. Noah, who drew the Scholar (4), is the Official (2), with 87. Clark, who drew the Official (2), is the Gentry (3), with 60. Reina, who drew the throne (1), is the Scholar (4), with 165.
